subject: LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value

messages.author: 3ba04b1c6505e8f9
messages.subject: LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value
parts:
Hello,

I am attempting to obtain the LOD support interval using function 'lodint'. My peak LOD value for the chromosome is 5.1, so I would expect the support interval to include markers of LOD 3.6 or higher (if I interpret correctly the meaning of a 1.5-drop LOD score...). When I perform the 'lodint' function, I obtain flanking markers of 3.32 and 2.80 LOD at either end of the QTL region, which is a lower threshold than I would anticipate based on my QTL peak value.

I have included my code below. [Sidenote* My QTL plots include an LOD threshold line of 3.91, as that was the significance value obtained after 1000 permutations testing].

Thank you for any insights you could provide!

Cheers,
David 

#CIM for trait
out1_cim.em <- cim(mapthis, pheno.col = (1), n.marcovar=1, method=c("em"), map.function=c("kosambi"))

#Regression for trait
summary(out1_cim.em, threshold=3.91)
mapthis <- sim.geno(mapthis, n.draws=128)
qtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- makeqtl(mapthis, chr=c(1), pos=c(213)) 
summary(out.qtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, pheno.col=1, formula=y~Q1))
plot(qtl_traitA_avg_chr1)

#fit the model (with QTL in fixed positions)
out.fq_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1)
summary(out.fq_traitA_avg_chr1)

#refine QTL and plot LOD profile
rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1 <- refineqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1, verbose=FALSE)
rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1
out.fq2_traitA_avg_chr1 <- fitqtl(mapthis, qtl=qtl_traitA_avg_chr1, formula=y~Q1, dropone=FALSE)
summary(out.fq2_traitA_avg_chr1)
plotLodProfile(rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1)
abline(3.91, 0, untf = FALSE)
title(main = "Trait A")

#obtain LOD support interval
lodint(rqtl_traitA_avg_chr1, chr, qtl.index=1, drop=1.5, lodcolumn=1, expandtomarkers=FALSE)

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LOD support interval does not match expected 1.5-drop LOD value
parts:
The endpoints of the support interval that lodint (with drop=1.5) calculates are the left- and right-most positions on the chromosome where the LOD score is within 1.5 of the maximum. If there are multiple peaks, they all get merged together.

karl
